evidence: image col 4-5: '唐書李華傳華文辭緜麗著吊古戰場文極思丨丨' with no attribution after it. The English adds '<note>From Zhao Kuang.</note>' here and also after the Du Fu passage. The only 趙 on the page is in '…亦盡丨丨況趙乎' (col 2-3, 'how much more so Zhao'), part of Liu Kezhuang's postscript; there is no 匡/Kuang anywhere. The first note also misattributes: 'From Liu Kezhuang's postscript' is put on the Han Yu line, when the postscript is the source of the following Du Fu supplementary-annotations quote. A reader is given false sources for the quotations. The claim is slightly too broad: 趙 does appear on the page, but 'Zhao Kuang' as a source does not.

image: two short entries, '銀鋌 魏書崔浩傳 見金鋌下' and '銀繭 馬祖常贈客詩丨丨霞巳積翠幢柏方遮'. Stored OCR: '是毛魏書崔浩專 / 金金見金鋌下 / 銀 / 繭 / 霞馬 / 巳祖 / 積常 / 翠贈 / 幢客 / 柏詩 / 方 / 遮'. The 銀鋌 headword is lost ('是毛'), and the 銀繭 citation's two columns are interleaved one character at a time, so neither Ma Zuchang nor his line can be read.

From the interleaved fragments the English makes seven headings: 'Silver… / Cocoon… / Rosy Clouds and Horses… / Ancestral Sacrifice… / Accumulated Emerald Banners… / Cypress Square… / Shielding…'. The page has one entry, 銀繭 (silver cocoon), citing Ma Zuchang's 贈客詩 '銀繭霞巳積，翠幢柏方遮'. The English also gives the 銀鋌 entry as 'Mao Weishu states that Cui Hao specialized in [text missing]', when the image reads only 魏書崔浩傳 見金鋌下. A reader sees invented headwords and no Ma Zuchang.

image: '日照香爐生丨丨遙看瀑布挂前川'. OCR: '日照香爐生\n遙看瀑布挂前川'. The 丨丨 marks are dropped all through the OCR, often replaced by a line break. The omission is real, but it is recoverable: the headword is printed large at the head of each entry (雲煙, 凌煙, 輕煙, 翠煙, and the previous page's 紫煙), and the reader-facing English restores it everywhere ('generating purple smoke', 'into the cloud smoke', 'Lingyan Pavilion'). A reader of the page is not misled about what each quotation says. This is a systematic OCR omission, not a serious misreading.

image cols 7-8: '…馬皇見迎於護龍 / 操煙 晏子五尺童子丨寸之丨天下不能足以[新序?]…今君之左右皆丨丨之徒而君終不知 / 輕煙 新論…'. OCR: '馬皇見迎操煙 / 晏子五尺童子 / 寸之 / 天下不能足以 / 新 / 諱龍 / 於謨龍 / 斬 / 今君之左右皆 / 之徒而君終不知'. 於護龍 is split and misread as '諱龍 / 於謨龍'; a stray '斬' is added; the 操煙 headword runs into the previous citation; and the 新論 source label becomes separate '新 / 論' lines. The 操煙 entry and its citations cannot be read.

English: 'New <unclear>...</unclear> taboo name Long <unclear>...</unclear> Yu Mo Long <unclear>...</unclear> Behead. Now those surrounding you are all <unclear>cloud smoke</unclear> followers'. 'taboo name', 'Yu Mo Long' and 'Behead' are translations of OCR garbage (護龍 read as 諱龍/謨龍, plus the stray 斬). The image has no taboo name and no beheading. The 操煙 headword is never given, and the passage is attributed to no source. Some of it is marked unclear, but invented content ('Behead', 'taboo name') is presented as text from the source.

image: '…徙丨丨道宣慰司治潭州…道在丨丨為屬州丨丨楊公又賢也…萬里丨丨月…' followed by the large headword '湖北'. This is volume 53 (lake 湖 compounds), and Han Yu's 送何堅序 reads '道於湖南為屬州，湖南楊公又賢也'; the Yuan office is 湖南道宣慰司. So the headword is 湖南 (Hunan). The English renders it 'Xiang River' in every instance, and a note asserts 'The original text uses a placeholder 丨丨 to represent the headword Xiang-jiang'. A reader is misled about the headword and its administrative sense. Class note: the OCR is not garbled here (the marks are the standard convention), so this is a wrongly resolved headword plus an invented note (T10), not strictly fluent-over-garble (T7). The error itself is as claimed.

image: '川日 劉長卿赤沙湖詩沙鷗[丨丨] / 積暮雪丨丨動寒暉', a single citation. OCR gives '川 / 劉長卿赤沙湖詩沙鷗 / 川 / 曰 / 劉 / 少 / 湖 / 詩 / 沙 / 鷗 / 尺 / 暉 / 川日積暮雪——動寒暉'. The citation is read once correctly, then again as shredded single characters ('劉 少 湖 詩 沙 鷗 尺 暉', with 長→少 and 赤沙→少湖).

English: 'Liu Shaohu, in a poem: The sand gulls reflect the river sun. <note>The text repeats a similar line attributed to different poets.</note> Chi Hui, in a poem: The evening snow accumulates on the river sun…'. The image has only Liu Changqing's 赤沙湖詩 ('沙鷗丨丨積暮雪 丨丨動寒暉'). 'Liu Shaohu' and 'Chi Hui' are poets made from the shredded fragments (劉/少/湖, 尺/暉), and the note falsely claims the source repeats the line under another poet.

image: '浦迥 李端詩城閣烟草遍丨丨雪林分', one citation of Li Duan, 'mist and grass cover the distant shore; snowy woods divide'. Because the OCR split it ('遍 / 雪林分'), the English makes a second poet: 'Xue Lin, in a poem: Dividing the river shore, distant and separated.' There is no poet Xue Lin on the page; 雪林 means 'snowy woods' in Li Duan's line.

image col 8: '宋史河渠志兩渠溉田凡四萬四千五百頃', which is 44,500 qing. The stored OCR is correct ('凡四萬四千 / 五百頃'). The English says 'a total of 4,450,000 qing', a hundredfold inflation of a historical figure. This is a translation error, not an OCR numeral error (O7 is an OCR class), so the class label should change; the error itself is real and serious as stated.
